attempts.label: CRCNS:ssc-10
attempts.entry_title: Tactile enrichment and the whisker map in L2/3 and L4 of mouse S1 (LeMessurier et al. 2019)
attempts.summary: The findings that enrichment sharpens L2/3 receptive fields, steepens the drop in correlations at column boundaries and improves decoding of whisker identity held up here, though some correlation and decoder values fall below the paper's. The stronger L2/3 response to a column's own whisker held only with the data set's stored responsiveness p-values, which come from a test other than the Methods describe. The rise in L2/3 cells tuned to the column whisker did not reproduce: the paper does not describe its test of equivalent best whiskers, and the main reading puts 91.7% of normally housed cells near the column centre in that group, against 67%. In L4, weaker surround responses held; a weaker column-whisker response did not.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of LeMessurier, Laboy-Juarez, McLain, Chen, Nguyen and Feldman (2019) on CRCNS data set ssc-10, which holds the 2-photon calcium imaging of L2/3 (Drd3-Cre) and L4 (Scnn1a-Cre) neurons in enriched and normally housed mice during deflection of nine whiskers. It covers cell counts, the point representation, tuning to the columnar whisker, receptive fields, signal and noise correlations, neuropil robustness and decoding. The juxtacellular recordings of Figure 1F are not in the data set.

With per-field means (11 fields per group) no size reaches p < 0.001 (p = 0.024 to 0.42); the pooled ensembles reuse the same ROIs within a field.

findings.statement: The cell-attached recordings with simultaneous GCaMP6s imaging (Figure 1F, 10 L2/3 cells in 5 C57BL/6 mice) are not in the data set.

No barrel areas or radii are stored. ROI_pos_barrel_norm divides each position by a radius along the ROI's direction (the ratio to ROI_pos_barrel varies by a median 37% within a barrel), and the radii used are not given.

processed_data.mat holds more ROIs than reduced_data.mat in 21 of 36 fields (1044 against 998 NH L2/3, 1276 against 1147 EN L2/3, 464 against 362 NH L4, 782 against 615 EN L4), with no list of the excluded ROIs or the reason. The paper reports 1257 EN L2/3, 322 NH L4 and 586 EN L4 cells, which match neither count.
sponTrace keeps fewer blank trials than Stimuli marks blank (for example 51 of 61 in DNH15b/20170502/f1), with no stated rule.
The code of Stimuli.Label is not described: label k is whisk{k+1} of settings.mat for k = 0 to 8 and 9 is a blank trial, which agrees with the per-whisker frame lists in every field.

Field DNH13b/20161208/f2 has no trials for whiskers E1, E2 and E3 (absent from traceByStim, Stimuli frame lists and permTestResults), which the descriptor does not mention; it also lacks positions for three barrels.

Movie names carry a leading m in Stimuli and not in deltaF in some fields, and the other way in others; three fields (DENR2b/20160408, DNH15a/20170505/f1, DENR15b/20170513/f1) have one dF/F movie with no Stimuli entry.

The stored L4 dF/F (npSub = 1) is reproduced (within 0.012) only by filtering the ROI and neuropil traces with the 5-frame median before subtracting 0.3 of the neuropil, as the data descriptor says; the Methods describe the subtraction from the raw ROI fluorescence and do not give the order.

In three L4 fields (ScENR10c/20180104/f1, ScENR10c/20180110, ScENR10b/20180105/f2) sponTrace holds 76-frame segments starting 0.5 s after each blank onset, where every other field, and traceByStim everywhere, hold 106 frames starting 0.5 s before onset. Read as the other fields, the blank-trial baseline and evoked windows fall 0.5 s late.

disagreements.reason: The criterion's own partial clause needs both 0-75 um values within tolerance and both absence tests non-significant. Under E1 and E2 the eBW test is significant (p = 0.036 and 0.0051; cell 61). Under E3 the test is not significant, but the L4 value is 82.1% against 73 +/- 7.3. So no reading meets the partial clause; figs2-1 and fig4ae fail their partial clauses in the same way and are scored not reproduced. The verifier retracts its round-1 recommendation of partial.

After the re-run every condition of the criterion holds in both responsiveness readings (cell 110): EN is lower outside for signal and noise (p <= 0.0016), signal inside is not lower (p = 0.39 and 0.19), and the EN - NH difference is more negative outside, for noise -0.0454 against -0.0450 and -0.0430 against -0.0409. The round-1 reason, that the Methods reading failed by 0.0002, is no longer true. The added permutation test (p = 0.96 and 0.81) is a fair caveat for the notes, but it is not in the criterion, and the claims file decides the outcome. The criterion's weakness, comparing two differences without a test, should be reported against the claims file.

paper_notes.statement: The stored dF/F is reproduced (within 0.02) by a 5-frame moving median and F0 the 5th percentile of each movie, as the pipeline code does, not by the Methods' 4-frame median and 20th percentile.

The stored permTestResults come from a two-sided permutation test on medians (permTestType 'median' in every field), not the Methods' one-sided test on means. The two give the same responsive/unresponsive call for 86% of ROIs, and several EN effects reach significance only with the stored p-values.

Question for the authors. How were equivalent best whiskers tested? Neither the Methods nor the linked code give it (whiskPref is loaded precomputed). Permutation tests of the difference in means against the BW at p >= 0.05, with or without BH correction, or of medians, put the CW among the eBWs for 90-96% of NH L2/3 cells within 75 um of a column centre (paper 67%) and 85-88% of NH L2/3 cells within columns (paper 65%), while the NH L4 value matches (75.0%, paper 73%). Requiring each equivalent whisker also to be a significantly responsive whisker gives 73-75% and 72-74%, near the paper's values. Was that requirement part of the test?

Question for the authors. Which responsiveness test gave the cells analysed: the Methods' one-sided test on means, or the stored two-sided test on medians? The L2/3 cell counts match either, and no reading matches the L4 counts, but the L2/3 point representation (Figure 2A), the CW and surround responses (Figure 4B) and the CW response (Figure 4D) are significant only with the stored p-values.

Question for the authors. Is the spontaneous activity of Figure 4C the median dF/F on blank trials with or without subtracting the 0.5 s baseline? With it, EN L2/3 activity is higher than NH; without it, lower, as the paper reports.

entries.title: Tactile enrichment and the whisker map in L2/3 and L4 of mouse S1 (LeMessurier et al. 2019)
entries.description: Tests the findings of LeMessurier, Laboy-Juarez, McLain, Chen, Nguyen and Feldman (2019) on CRCNS data set ssc-10, which holds the 2-photon calcium imaging of L2/3 (Drd3-Cre) and L4 (Scnn1a-Cre) neurons in enriched and normally housed mice during deflection of nine whiskers. It covers cell counts, the point representation, tuning to the columnar whisker, receptive fields, signal and noise correlations, neuropil robustness and decoding. The juxtacellular recordings of Figure 1F are not in the data set.
